title: Custom IAM policies must allow CreateVolume from snapshots (#2190)

detection.reason: the controller's IAM policy is AWS-side; IRSA shows only the role ARN and EKS Pod Identity nothing at all

quote: Due to an upcoming change in handling of IAM polices for the CreateVolume API when creating a volume from an EBS snapshot, a change to your EBS CSI Driver policy may be needed.
remediation: If the controller's role uses the AWS-managed AmazonEBSCSIDriverPolicy, nothing to do (AWS updated it in every partition on 2025-01-13). With a custom policy, apply the change in GitHub issue #2190: CreateVolume from a snapshot is now authorized against the snapshot resource as well, so add a statement allowing ec2:CreateVolume on arn:aws:ec2:*:*:snapshot/* with no tag condition (upstream's example policy). Upstream: this applies to every driver version, upgraded or not.
verifyCommand: kubectl get sa -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name == "ebs-csi-controller-sa") | "\(.metadata.namespace): \(.metadata.annotations["eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn"] // "no IRSA annotation")"'  # prints the controller's IRSA role; with none, aws eks list-pod-identity-associations --cluster-name CLUSTER_NAME --service-account ebs-csi-controller-sa names the Pod Identity role; list its policies with aws iam list-attached-role-policies --role-name ROLE_NAME

title: v1.38.0 images were promoted incorrectly — do not run them

detection.reason: read from the image TAG of the ebs-csi-controller / ebs-csi-node workloads — a digest-pinned image (@sha256:…) or a mirror that renames the tag is not resolved and reads clean

quote: Do not use any images from `v1.38.0` and upgrade directly to `v1.38.1`.
remediation: Move every EBS CSI workload off v1.38.0 — straight to v1.38.1 or the target version. Upstream: the v1.38.0 images were promoted incorrectly due to a process error; v1.38.1 differs from it only by golang.org/x/crypto v0.30.0 -> v0.31.0.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy,ds -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("^ebs-csi-(controller|node(-.+)?)$")) | .metadata.namespace as $n | .metadata.name as $w | .spec.template.spec.containers[] | select(.name == "ebs-plugin") | "\($n)/\($w): \(.image)"'  # a tag of v1.38.0 is the recalled build

title: EBS CSI metrics renamed (aws_ebs_csi_ prefix, _total, seconds) — dashboards and alerts on the old names go blank

detection.reason: dashboards, recording rules and alerts live outside the cluster inventory

quote: The controller plugin metrics now use the prefix `aws_ebs_csi_` instead of `cloudprovider_aws_`.
remediation: Rewrite dashboards, recording rules and alerts: controller metrics move from cloudprovider_aws_* to aws_ebs_csi_* — not a pure prefix swap: cloudprovider_aws_api_throttled_requests_total -> aws_ebs_csi_api_request_throttles_total, cloudprovider_aws_api_request_errors -> aws_ebs_csi_api_request_errors_total, cloudprovider_aws_api_request_duration_seconds -> aws_ebs_csi_api_request_duration_seconds; node (NVMe) metrics gain the aws_ebs_csi_ prefix and a _total suffix on counters, and their time units change from microseconds to seconds (divide old thresholds by 1,000,000). From v1.41 the old controller names are off unless the controller runs --deprecated-metrics=true, and from v1.42 the node service no longer serves controller metrics.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy,ds -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("^ebs-csi-(controller|node(-.+)?)$")) | .metadata.namespace as $n | .metadata.name as $w | .spec.template.spec.containers[] | select(.name == "ebs-plugin") | select($w == "ebs-csi-controller") | "\($n)/\($w): \(.args | join(" "))"'  # --http-endpoint means metrics are scraped (rename dashboards); --deprecated-metrics=true keeps the old names until it is removed
coversNotes: URGENT (1.38.1): Node plugin metrics have been renamed to follow Prometheus best practices
URGENT (1.38.1): Changed time units from microseconds to seconds for all counters
Confirm metrics to Prometheus best practices

title: Kustomize installs: VolumeAttributesClass is on by default (extra errors without the feature gate)

detection.reason: which install method rendered the workloads is not collected, nor the control plane's feature gates

quote: If you are deploying using the Kustomize manifests on a cluster that does not have the `VolumeAttributesClass` feature gate enabled on the control plane, you may see harmless extra failures related to the feature in the csi-provisioner and/or csi-resizer logs.
remediation: Only for installs built from the upstream Kustomize overlays: on Kubernetes before 1.34 (VolumeAttributesClass not GA) expect VolumeAttributesClass errors in csi-provisioner / csi-resizer logs; they are harmless. Do not chase them as an upgrade failure.
